title: Evidence Automation & SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Control Mapping — RBAC v2, Audit Logs, SIEM Export (Gap Analysis)
content:
Executive summary:
This working doc maps current RBAC v2, audit log schema, evidence automation pipelines, and SIEM export practices to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls. Purpose is to (1) identify gaps that prevent automated evidence collection and auditor readiness, (2) prioritize remediation with owners and ETA, and (3) prepare short-answer Q&A for external auditors. This is a draft for internal review — expect follow-ups after engineering scoping.

Scope:
- Systems in-scope: Redwood hosted control plane, Dedicated control plane telemetry, Private deployment control-plane connectors (where we ship a collector).
- Components: RBAC v2 (roles, resource scoping, policy change audit trail), centralized audit log schema (authz/authn events, config changes, admin actions, rollouts), evidence automation (S3-backed bundles + md5 checksums + immutable storage), SIEM export pipeline (Kafka -> SIEM connector).

Current state (summary):
- RBAC v2: fine-grained roles implemented; role templates for Developer/Operator/Admin. Policy changes are versioned in GitOps repo; UI changes emit events but not all are tagged with requestor IP/client metadata. No standardized change reason metadata.
- Audit log schema: JSON lines with timestamp, actor_id, session_id, action, resource, outcome, request_id. Missing fields: actor_ip, invoking_service, before/after config diff for policy updates.
- Evidence automation: nightly snapshot job composes evidence bundles per control area (IAM changes, user provisioning, vulnerability scans). Bundles are S3 objects with metadata file and checksum. Retrieval API exists but is manual (requests to compliance-ops).
- SIEM export: real-time export via Kafka topic redwood.audit -> LogForwarder -> customer SIEM; export includes redacted payloads for PII. Sampling is applied to high-volume routes (defaults to 10%).

Control mapping (high level):
- SOC 2 CC6 / ISO A.9 (Access control): map to RBAC enforcement + role review evidence. Auditor wants: role definitions, access reviews, recent changes, proof of approval.
- SOC 2 CC7 / ISO A.12 (Change management & logging): map to audit logs for config and deployment changes, signed build artifacts, and rollouts.
- SOC 2 CC8 / ISO A.10 (Encryption & key management): map to KMS usage for evidence storage and S3 encryption; key rotation proof.
- SOC 2 CC5 / ISO A.16 (Incident mgmt): map to alerting/incident tickets + SIEM escalations.

Gap analysis (findings prioritized):
1) Missing requestor metadata on RBAC policy-change events (Severity: High). Impact: auditors require proof of who approved/initiated changes. Current mitigation: GitOps PR history exists but not correlated in audit log.
2) No before/after diffs in audit entries for policy/config changes (Severity: High). Impact: harder to demonstrate change rationale and scope.
3) Evidence retrieval is manual and ad-hoc (Severity: Medium). Impact: delay when auditors request longitudinal evidence; increases cost.
4) SIEM export sampling on security-relevant routes (Severity: Medium). Impact: may fail auditor sampling tests for completeness.
5) Log integrity attestation missing (signed/immutable logs) (Severity: High). Impact: auditors expect tamper-evidence for critical logs.
6) Retention policy mapping to ISO/SOC requirements not fully documented for Dedicated/Private tenants (Severity: Medium).

Recommended remediation (short):
- G1 (owner: eng-security; ETA: 6 weeks): Add actor_ip, invoking_service, change_reason, and git_pr_id to audit log schema for all policy-change events. Backfill mapping where possible (cross-link with GitOps).
- G2 (owner: infra; ETA: 8 weeks): Emit before/after diffs for resource-level config changes into the audit stream as compact JSON patch (or attach patch id).
- G3 (owner: compliance-ops + infra; ETA: 4 weeks): Implement an evidence automation API that creates timeboxed, signed bundles on demand (not just nightly). Integrate this with the auditor portal for secure download (2FA + expiring links).
- G4 (owner: platform-engineering; ETA: 12 weeks): Remove sampling for security-relevant log topics; introduce dynamic throttling and intelligent batching to keep costs down.
- G5 (owner: sre; ETA: 10 weeks): Add WORM/S3-object-lock policy for critical audit log archives; produce signed manifests (SHA256) and register manifests in a ledger for retention proofs.
- G6 (owner: product-hosted-api; ETA: 6 weeks): Publish retention mapping doc per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and link to policy (Confluence).

Evidence automation design notes (proposed architecture):
- Trigger model: API-triggered bundles plus scheduled snapshots. Request parameters: scope (control area), timeframe, requester, justification.
- Bundle contents: logs (compressed), config snapshots, GitOps PR exports, role membership CSV, signatures/manifest (sha256), manifest-signer (KMS id).
- Storage: encrypted S3 prefix per audit request with object-lock for required retention period. Metadata catalog stored in Redshift for rapid search.
- Access: short-lived pre-signed URL generated by evidence service; requires 2FA and ticket id; expiration 7 days by default.

SIEM export & schema requirements (auditor-focused):
- Minimal required fields to satisfy control audits: timestamp, request_id, actor_id, actor_type, actor_ip, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, before_id (if patch), diff_reference, git_pr_id, tenant_id, region, signature (log-integrity id).
- Recommended naming conventions: event.source = "redwood.control-plane", event.type = "auditable_change" or "authn"/"authz"; use RFC3339 timestamps.
- Export reliability: replace sampling with adaptive sampling and cardinality reduction (truncate large payload but attach diff_reference). Provide a completeness metric (percent of expected events emitted).

Auditor Q&A prep (anticipated questions + suggested short answers):
- Q: How do you prove who changed RBAC policies?
  A: All policy changes are captured as GitOps PRs (contains author, approvals) and correlated to control-plane audit events via git_pr_id. We will extend the event schema to include actor_ip and change_reason and publish a cross-link report.

- Q: Can you demonstrate log immutability and non-repudiation?
  A: We store critical archives using S3 Object Lock (WORM) and sign daily manifests with KMS keys. Manifests are hashed and registered in an internal ledger. Planned: produce auditor-facing attestation package with signed manifests.

- Q: How do you ensure log completeness when forwarding to customer SIEMs?
  A: We forward all auditable events to a central Kafka topic and have a LogForwarder that delivers to SIEMs with exactly-once semantics. For high-volume routes we will remove sampling for security events and implement buffering/backpressure detection and signal completeness metrics to compliance.

- Q: How does the evidence retrieval process work?
  A: Compliance-ops or authorized auditor requests a bundle via API; the evidence service collates required artifacts, signs the manifest, places a timeboxed artifact in S3 and provides a short-lived download link. Admin approval and 2FA required.

- Q: What is the retention policy for logs and evidence?
  A: Retention mapping is defined per deployment mode; hosted: 7 years for critical audit archives, 1 year for operational logs. Dedicated/Private: configurable but recommended default mirrors hosted. We will publish an official retention matrix in Confluence.

Mock Q&A snippets (for auditors):
- Auditor: show me the RBAC change for project X on 2025-11-02.
  Prep: provide GitOps PR URL, audit log event (with git_pr_id & before/after diff_reference), signed evidence bundle id.

- Auditor: supply proof of key rotation for evidence-signer KMS.
  Prep: provide KMS key rotation logs, KMS key policy change audit, signed manifests before/after rotation.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require full before/after diffs inline in event or only a diff_reference? (ops: space & cost tradeoffs)
- Sampling policy thresholds: define routes classified as security-sensitive.
- Evidence portal scope: third-party auditor self-service or ticketed access only?

Next steps / action items (short):
- This week: align on schema additions (actor_ip, git_pr_id, change_reason) - owner: eng-security (due 2026-02-17).
- 2 weeks: infra to prototype signed manifest flow and object-lock staging bucket (POC).
- 4 weeks: compliance-ops and infra build on-demand evidence API and add audit portal mockups.

Appendix: quick checklist for auditor readiness (pre-delivery):
- Role definitions exported (CSV) + active membership snapshot.
- GitOps PR history for last 12 months for role/policy changes.
- Audit log export (signed) for requested timeframe with completeness metric.
- Evidence bundle with manifest and KMS-signed signature.
- SIEM ingest configuration and delivery logs (proof of forwarding).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft intended for cross-team scoping. Please add comments inline in Confluence Control Matrix (linked) and file follow-up JIRA tasks for any items that impact your roadmap.
